newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Cambodia's Ranariddh arrives in Jakarta.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Ranariddh arrives in Jakarta.

text.p: Ousted Cambodian First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh arrived in Jakarta on Wednesday as part of efforts to drum up international support against his rival Hun Sen.

An Indonesian foreign ministry official with the protocol division said Ranariddh arrived from Singapore and took a helicopter from the airport into the city, avoiding reporters and camera crews waiting for him at the terminal.

His arrival coincided with a meeting in Kuala Lumpur of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) at which Cambodia's neighbours rejected a last-minute plea by the Hun Sen government to join the regional grouping.
Sources at the presidential palace said Ranariddh was likely to meet President Suharto later on Wednesday although no time for a meeting had been set.
The Cambodian leader, ousted from his post by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen two weeks ago, had said on Monday that he planned to visit Indonesia.
Jakarta was a co-chairman of the 1991 Paris talks that ended decades of bloodshed in Cambodia and laid the ground for United Nations-sponsored elections in 1993.

Ranariddh won the poll and agreed to an uneasy power-sharing coalition with Hun Sen -- a merger that crumbled earlier this month when Hun Sen's forces ousted royalist troops loyal to Ranariddh in a bloody putsch in Phnom Penh.
ASEAN held a special ceremony in Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday to welcome new members Burma and Laos but opted to continue to postpone Cambodia's membership indefinitely.

Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot, who has been named to replace Ranariddh as first prime minister, had told reporters in Kuala Lumpur earlier in the day that Phnom Penh wanted to reverse its previous hardline stance and join ASEAN, asking it to mediate in the conflict between the warring prime ministers.
